seal.statement: Every proof the gate and continuous integration perform is produced once per push cycle and read everywhere else: each repository-health metric (complexity, cognitive complexity, import cycles, duplication, file size, unused exports) has one producing command whose report every consumer reads; the fixed test lists (the safety spine and the focused contracts) are one list run once; the sealed import graph has one producer and one reader that binds the seal; every whole-tree check declares the inputs that trigger it and runs only when they changed, in the shape of the existing full-corpus triggers; ESLint covers exactly the files of the pushed range at the pushed sha; repository-health's work is coalesced into the exact-sha ci run or removed; a proof-obligation registry extending the impact-contract registry is the one place an obligation (a fixed test, a whole-tree check, a witness) is declared with its inputs; the runner size, lane parallelism and timeouts of every workflow job follow a committed execution plan rather than per-workflow literals; and the behavioural canary is activated only when the gated run did not already run the whole corpus, with ci and repository-health under concurrency groups; the budget rows duplicate_metric_productions, duplicate_fixed_test_runs, import_graph_seal_readers_beyond_one, whole_tree_checks_without_input_trigger, eslint_off_pushed_range, repository_health_not_coalesced, workflows_without_concurrency, ci_resources_not_plan_driven and canary_after_full_corpus read zero, and every reduction cites the measurement it is compared against.

text: Identity gap exposed by the new identity line during the publish of d9819d43e: the publisher's synthetic ref line 'HEAD <head> refs/heads/main <remoteBefore>' carried the string 'undefined' as the remote base (pre-push printed 'against main base undefined'), so the hook's cat-file guard rejected it and the change proof resolved the publication merge-base itself. Harmless today (the merge-base of origin/main and HEAD is the remote main the publisher just verified) and pre-existing, but the proof base should be the exact remote sha the publisher read; owner: scripts/publish-head.js remoteBefore plumbing into gateExactHead. Route: fix with the pushed-range eslint row of this quest, which touches the same ref-line contract.

The duplicate-metric row measures the wrong thing. The sealed statement says each metric has ONE PRODUCING COMMAND whose report every consumer reads; the row as landed counts SURFACES that mention a checker, so a gate and a CI job that both invoke the single producer would count as a duplicate, and the row could only reach zero by leaving one of them unmeasured. The measured surfaces today: complexity, cognitive complexity and cycles each on three surfaces, duplication on two, file size on five (pre-commit staged, pre-push corpus worktree, static audits, owner-debt refresh, repository-health), unused exports on two. Read as commands instead: the owner-debt refresh spawns check-complexity, check-cognitive-complexity, check-circular-dependencies and check-duplication to write its reports, and run-static-audits re-runs the same four through npm run test:complexity and test:metrics; pre-push re-runs cycles and unused-exports; pre-commit and the corpus worktree re-run file size. Correcting the row to count distinct producing commands per metric is a repair of the instrument to match the sealed claim, not a widening of it.

Correcting the previous finding: the row is sound as written and no supersession is needed. The gate and the ci workflow do not name the checkers; they run npm run test:owner-debt:prepare, which expands to the inventory generator, and the generator's own command table (scripts/global-owner-debt-inventory/constants.js) is the surface that spawns check-complexity, check-cognitive-complexity, check-circular-dependencies and check-duplication. So one producing command reached from many surfaces counts once, and the row reaches zero exactly when each metric is computed by one surface and every other consumer reads that surface's report: the refresh for the four, the corpus worktree for file size, and one site for unused exports. The reductions are therefore: coalesce repository-health (it recomputes all six after the gate already did), make run-static-audits read the reports instead of re-running test:complexity and test:metrics, and let the pre-push cycles and unused-exports stages read the refresh's reports.

SUPERSEDED by owner decision 2026-09-14 (R09): the sealed statement's single-production clause and the duplicate_metric_productions row move to a new quest, single-metric-production. Why: making a consumer read a report instead of recomputing a metric is derived material standing in for its producer (R05), so it is sound only if the report records the source digest it was produced from and every consumer verifies that digest or refuses; that is a redesign of six checkers and of the gate's command ordering (the post-push manifest runs the static audits BEFORE the owner-debt refresh, and the refresh the gate runs is --refresh-import-graph-only, so no metric report exists at that point), and it deserves its own design note and verifier rather than riding along with eight mechanical reductions. What remains in this quest is unchanged: the fixed test lists, the import-graph seal readers, the input-triggered whole-tree checks, the pushed-range eslint, the repository-health coalescing, the workflow concurrency, the plan-driven resources and the canary activation. The new quest inherits the measured figure: twelve productions beyond the first across complexity, cognitive complexity, cycles, duplication, file size and unused exports.

Eight rows to zero, no metric production touched (that clause is superseded into single-metric-production). Fixed test lists: the four tests the safety spine already runs left the postpush manifest's focused-contracts command, so each runs once per gate. Import-graph seal: the seal-binds-graph predicate has one owner (sealBindsGraph, exported from scripts/checks/helper-import-closure.js) and now compares every digest the seal carries, not three of four; scripts/checks/impact-proof-cone-inputs.js and scripts/solve/guards.js consume it instead of deciding for themselves, and the helper-import-closure witness gained the two digests the real producer writes plus a case per digest proving drift refuses. Input triggers: test/manifests/proof-obligations.json declares, for each of the 27 whole-tree commands the gate runs, the repository paths whose change makes it meaningful. ESLint: the hook's lint stage lints the pushed range (base..HEAD, remote base of the pushed ref) and falls back to every tracked file only when there is no range to diff; measured on a real range, 17 files, clean. Repository health: the workflow is deleted and its steps are a continue-on-error job inside ci.yml, on main pushes only, so the two signals stay distinguishable (red gate = unproved, red health = structural debt) and the red-main guard still reads only the gate. Concurrency: ci (cancel superseded pull-request runs, never a main push), full-gate (per sha) and the health job's former workflow. Resources: test/manifests/ci-resource-plan.json decides the runner and timeout of all 13 workflow jobs and the row refuses any job whose literals differ or that the plan does not know. Canary: it now triggers on the ci run's completion rather than on the push, a decide job reads the gate run's proof-scope artifact (ci records whether its proof ran the whole corpus), and the corpus job runs only when the gate did not already prove it. Row instruments corrected while measuring: the budget script is not a seal reader (it names the markers it looks for), the eslint row reads the hook's lint stage rather than a substring anywhere in the file, and a module consuming the seal predicate is not a second reader. 22 suites green (179 assertions), witness 6/6 with met and offending fixtures, complexity 1822/1822, unused exports 1438/1438, eslint, ambient-intrinsics, literals and audit:shards clean.

r1 REJECT (category-complete). Blockers: (CL-1) test/release/project-hardening-contracts.test.js is a SAFETY-SPINE test and reads .github/workflows/repository-health.yml, so deleting that file turns every change proof and every CI run red; it also asserts the canary's on.push branches. It is one of the four tests this attempt moved out of focused-contracts, so the manifest's first command would have caught it in seconds. (C-1) the lint stage's LINT_BASE lets an ambient LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE win over the pushed ref, inverting the rule the hook states for the test stage; LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE=HEAD makes the range empty and eslint runs zero times while the row reads 0. (C-3) ci greps 'test stage: full-corpus' in npm run check, but that string exists only in push-gate-change-proof.js which CI never runs, so fullCorpus is always false and the proof-scope mechanism is a sensor reading a string its producer never emits. (C-4) the canary's checkout has no ref, so under workflow_run it checks out the default-branch tip at event time rather than the run's head_sha, and the sha recorded in proof-scope.json is never compared - a regression against the pushed-sha identity the previous quest established. (CL-2) whole-tree eslint now blocks nothing: the lint range does not include eslint.config.js or the package manifests, and the only remaining whole-tree lint is test:static inside the new continue-on-error health job. (S-1) the constraint says workflow lines move down, never up; they went 1231 to 1307. Also: the canary no longer runs when ci is red (it used to run on every main push), repository-health lost its manual dispatch, the obligations registry is declared but nothing consumes it so all 27 commands still run unconditionally and several declarations omit scripts/** (editing a checker would skip it), the eslint and canary rows are satisfiable by text that does not do the thing, and the stage manifest's lint prose is now wrong. Clean: the seal predicate (the producer always writes all four digests; strictly stricter, cannot over-refuse; no cycle), the fail-open decide step, concurrency groups, YAML validity, 24 suites, the registry and plan consistency, and every static check.

Corrective attempt after r1. CL-1: test/release/project-hardening-contracts.test.js is the contract, so it was re-expressed rather than worked around - it now reads the structural analysis as a step of ci's gate job (continue-on-error, not on pull requests, the three analyses present and the inventory before the analyses that read it, no behavioural suite) and demands that the canary trigger on ci's workflow_run and pin its checkout to workflow_run.head_sha; the helpers were extracted because the added claims pushed the function past the complexity ratchet. C-1: the lint stage takes the pushed ref's remote sha as its base and never an ambient LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE, the same rule the test stage states. CL-2: a change to eslint.config.js, package.json or package-lock.json relints every tracked file, because a per-file verdict holds only while the contract producing it is fixed. C-3: the scope is written by the run that decides it - select-change-tests.js records sha, kind, test count and fullCorpus false (that path never runs the corpus) and push-gate-change-proof.js records the escalation it decided - so nothing greps another process's log; ci only uploads the file. C-4: the canary checks out workflow_run.head_sha and its decide step requires the recorded sha to match before skipping. CL-3: the canary follows every completed gate run on main, red or green, because a red gate can be an unrelated intermittent and the corpus exists to find what a cone cannot. CL-4: ci gained workflow_dispatch and the health steps answer it. S-1: the structural analysis is now two non-blocking steps of the gate job rather than a second job, so there is one checkout and one install; with the headers rewritten to describe the arrangement that exists, workflow lines are 1231, exactly the figure at HEAD, no longer rising. RI-3: run-static-audits.js consumes the registry - an audit whose declared inputs the pushed range did not touch is skipped and printed as SKIP, and with no committed range every audit runs; every obligation now declares scripts/** because a checker's own implementation decides what it proves. RI-4: the canary row checks the wiring (workflows: [ci], workflow_run.head_sha, proof-scope) rather than words a comment could carry. S-2 and S-3: the stage manifest's lint prose, RELEASE.md's main-push row, check-fast-static's notes and the impact-contract description name the arrangement that exists. 29 suites green (259 assertions), 22 audits pass, witness 6/6, complexity 1822/1822, all eight rows 0, probe 0.

r2 REJECT. Fixed and verified: the spine contract test, the ambient lint base, the lint-contract widening, the scope written by the deciding run, the canary sha pin, manual dispatch, the doc drift, the canary row markers, and workflow lines at 1231 (equality, so never-up holds while move-down does not). Three blockers. (B-1) The canary's decide job still carries conclusion == 'success': my CL-3 edit targeted text that had already moved into the decide job, so the string replace matched nothing and silently did nothing, and the attempt record therefore asserts a change that is not in the tree - a red gate on a main sha still gets no corpus run. (B-2, new) Folding the structural analysis into the gate job puts it under that job's 120-minute timeout; step-level continue-on-error absorbs a failing step but not a job timeout, so analysis that the deleted workflow budgeted 90 minutes for can now kill the required run, turn main red and block every subsequent push - the exact failure the deleted header existed to prevent. (B-3, new) The registry's declarations do not cover what the checkers read, and because every obligation declares scripts/**, the skip never fires on a source push and fires totally on doc, CI, chart, quest or empty-range pushes: simulated against the committed registry, seven of nine such cases skip all 22 audits, including audit:doc-audience for AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, audit:doc-ascii for examples, audit:roadmap-authority for solve/quests, audit:documentation-current for CHANGELOG and charts, and every audit when LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE names an empty range. Also: the health.if assertion is a match rather than an equality, so inverting the condition onto pull requests keeps it green; nothing asserts the decide job's gating or the analysis's budget; the ordering assertion is a substring position a comment could invert; and the skip path is unexercised by the attempt that introduces it.

Corrective attempt after r2. B-1: the canary's decide job no longer filters on the gate run's conclusion, so every completed gate run on main is followed, red or green; the earlier edit had targeted text that had already moved into the decide job, so the replace matched nothing and the record claimed a change the tree did not carry - every edit in this attempt asserts its anchor before writing. B-2: the structural analysis carries timeout-minutes 45 of its own, because continue-on-error absorbs a failing step and never a job timeout, so an overrun can no longer kill the required run and block later pushes; the contract test now requires that bound. B-3: skipping is admissible only when every changed path in the range is declared by some obligation, so an undeclared path or an empty range runs all 22 audits, and the declarations gained the files their checkers actually read (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and DEBUGGING.md for doc-audience; examples and roadmap for doc-ascii; solve/quests for roadmap-authority and closure-ledger; CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, charts and ci for documentation-current; charts for current-capabilities; CHANGELOG for no-legacy-naming). Simulated against the committed registry, the seven cases r2 named now run everything or skip only audits that do not govern the change. The skip decision is exported and witnessed by test/scripts/static-audit-input-triggers.test.js (pattern matching, undeclared path, empty range, declared documentation change, source change, and every obligation declaring its checker's home), and the runner's entry point is guarded so importing it cannot run the audits. Contract assertions tightened as r2 asked: health.if is an equality rather than a mention, the analysis must carry a finite timeout, and the canary's corpus job must need the decide job, run only on its output, and carry no conclusion filter. Also removed the duplicated comment block left by the r1 job shape and restored the reports directory to the health evidence upload. Workflow lines 1229 against 1231 at HEAD, so the budget moves down. 30 suites green (265 assertions), 22 audits pass with the skip path witnessed, complexity 1822/1822, unused exports 1438/1438, all eight rows 0, probe 0.

Residuals recorded rather than fixed, from verification r3: (1) the gate job's 120-minute budget in the resource plan was not raised by the 45 the structural analysis now occupies, so the proof's own headroom is roughly halved (typically 53 to 73 minutes remain after a bounded install); the plan holds literals, not a ratchet, so raising it later is a plan edit, and a cone large enough to need more than that would escalate to the whole corpus anyway. (2) The analysis is bounded at 45 where the deleted workflow budgeted 90, so an analysis that legitimately needs more is cut off and, under continue-on-error, the lane goes silently empty rather than red; if that happens the bound is the thing to raise, not the continue-on-error to remove. (3) The eslint and seal-reader rows keep their textual weakness: each can read zero for a hook or module that carries the right words without doing the thing, which is why the behavioural witnesses (the hook control-flow test, the seal drift cases) are the load-bearing proof and the rows are only the budget's view of them. (4) On a [ci:self-hosted] push the analysis depends on that box carrying a JRE, because the toolchain install step is hosted-only; under continue-on-error that is noise, not a gate.

Corrective attempt after r3, data and guard only. The two whole-tree greps declare themselves as such: check-no-kiro-refs and check-no-legacy-naming grep every tracked file, so no input list could be complete for them, and the registry now carries wholeTree true which auditIsOwed always honours - a quest-note push, the repository's commonest shape, can no longer skip them. audit:documentation-current gained architecture, examples, models, solve, test and AGENTS.md, the roots its own SCAN_ROOTS names; audit:roadmap-authority gained solve/specs, which it reads beside solve/quests. Two witness cases added: a whole-tree grep is owed for a quest note, an architecture document, a chart value and CLAUDE.md; and an audit whose scan roots exceed its declaration is owed for those roots. The direct-invocation guard now realpaths both sides, because Node realpaths import.meta.url but leaves argv[1] as typed: invoked through an absolute symlinked path the command exited 0 having run nothing, and the same shape sits in push-gate-change-proof.js where it is not load-bearing; verified by running the script through a symlinked repository path, which now runs all 22. Residuals recorded on this log rather than fixed: the gate job's budget was not raised by the 45 minutes the analysis now occupies, the analysis is bounded at 45 where the deleted workflow budgeted 90, the eslint and seal-reader rows keep their textual weakness behind behavioural witnesses, and the self-hosted path depends on that box's JRE. 27 suites green (233 assertions), 22 audits pass, 8 witness cases for the skip decision, all eight rows 0, probe 0, workflow lines 1229 against 1231.

r4 APPROVE. Every blocker from r1 to r3 closed and re-verified on this tree: the whole-tree greps are never skipped (owed in all 19 admissible cases of a 23-case simulation against the shipped exports), documentation-current and roadmap-authority are owed for the roots they scan, the wholeTree flag only ever widens what is owed so a wrong true costs minutes and can never under-run, the realpathed guard runs the audits through a symlinked absolute path where r3 exited 0 having run nothing, and the witness cases assert the shipped predicate against the committed registry rather than restating it. 28 suites (237 assertions), 22 audits, all eight rows 0, workflow lines 1229 against 1231. Residual named and fixed after the verdict: audit:impact-contracts declared only src, test and scripts while two of its 142 contract owners live under architecture and one under wit, so an architecture-only push skipped the audit that checks every owner path exists; architecture and wit are now declared and two witness cases pin them. The four recorded residuals were reviewed and none blocks: the gate budget not raised by the 45 the analysis occupies, the 45 against the deleted workflow's 90, the two textual rows standing behind behavioural witnesses, and the self-hosted JRE dependency.

Follow-up for the epic, raised by verification r4 and not fixed here: nothing ties an obligation's declared inputs to its checker's actual scan scope, and four verification rounds found four instances by hand (doc-audience missing the root documents, doc-ascii missing examples, roadmap-authority missing solve/specs, documentation-current missing half its SCAN_ROOTS, impact-contracts missing architecture and wit). The class ends with a row or witness that reads each checker's own root constants and compares them to its declaration, with wholeTree as the escape hatch where no list can be complete. Until that exists, a declaration narrower than its checker is an under-run nothing detects, and the registry should be read as a claim needing a witness rather than as a fact.

The owner's split (2026-09-14) narrowed this quest's sealed statement and its doneWhen rows, and a sealed probe is immutable: the solver's own answer to a changed probe is to supersede the quest, which this entry does. Nothing about the work is withdrawn. The eight reductions are complete in the tree and independently verified over four rounds (r1 and r2 and r3 rejected with real blockers, r4 approved): the fixed test lists no longer overlap, the seal-binds-graph predicate has one owner comparing every digest the producer writes, the proof-obligation registry declares the inputs of all 27 whole-tree commands and run-static-audits now consumes it with skipping admissible only when every changed path is declared, the pre-push lint covers the pushed range with the whole tree on a lint-contract change, repository-health is a bounded non-blocking step of the exact-sha ci run rather than a second workflow, every workflow has a concurrency group, all 14 jobs take their runner and timeout from a committed plan, and the canary follows the gate run for the sha that run proved. Every budget row reads zero and the work lands as a direct commit citing this record; the single-production clause continues as the sealed quest single-metric-production.
